object.title: Incidence coloring conjecture for Cartesian products
object.statement:
Let a graph $G$ be a **$(\Delta+1)$-graph** if it admits an incidence coloring with $\Delta(G)+1$ colors, and let $\mathbin{\square}$ denote the Cartesian product of graphs. Let $H$ be a graph whose incidence chromatic number satisfies $\chi_i(H)\leq\Delta(H)+2$. **Incidence coloring conjecture for Cartesian products.** If $G$ is a $(\Delta+1)$-graph and $H$ satisfies $\chi_i(H)\leq\Delta(H)+2$, then 
$$
\chi_i(G\mathbin{\square}H)\leq\Delta(G\mathbin{\square}H)+2.
$$
 This would extend the classes of Cartesian products known to satisfy the Brualdi–Massey bound; the source proves the result under additional degree conditions, but leaves this general assertion as a belief.
object.source_name: Petr Gregor, Borut Lužar and Roman Soták, “On incidence coloring conjecture in Cartesian products of graphs”, arXiv:1505.04908 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04908

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

object.title: Ulam reconstruction conjecture for infinite graphs with non-isomorphic vertex-deleted subgraphs
object.statement:
Let $G$) be an infinite graph with vertex set $E$. For $x\in E$, write $G|E\setminus\{x\}$ for the subgraph induced by deleting $x$, and write $\sim$ for graph isomorphism. **Ulam reconstruction conjecture.** If

$$
\forall x \in E,\quad G|E\setminus\{x\}\nsim G|E,
$$

then $G$ is Ulam-reconstructible. This is one of several proposed sufficient conditions for reconstructibility of infinite graphs; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.
object.source_name: Mohamed Sghiar, “Mesure et action des i-permutations sur les multigraphes multicolores finis et inifinis”, arXiv:1506.08963 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08963

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

object.title: The pseudoloop lemma conjecture for smooth digraphs
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be an oligomorphic permutation group on a set $G$, and let $\mathbb{G}$ be a countable smooth digraph of algebraic length $1$ on $G$ that is invariant under $\mathcal{G}$. A **pseudoloop** is an edge obtained from a loop by applying elements of $\mathcal{G}$ to its endpoints. **Pseudoloop lemma conjecture.** Either $\mathbb{G}$ contains a pseudoloop, or $\mathbb{G}$ together with the orbits of $\mathcal{G}$ on finite tuples pp-interprets $\mathbb{K}_3$ with parameters, where $\mathbb{K}_3=(\{1,2,3\};\neq)$. This would generalize the finite loop lemma to the stated infinite, invariant-digraph setting; the conjecture is presented as open in the source.
object.source_name: Libor Barto and Michael Pinsker, “The algebraic dichotomy conjecture for infinite domain Constraint Satisfaction Problems”, arXiv:1602.04353 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.04353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

object.title: Sharp stability conjecture for the Erdős matching theorem
object.statement:
Let $s,k,n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy

$$
n\geq(s+1)k.
$$

Let $d\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq[n]^{(k)}$ have matching number $m(\mathcal{F})=s$. If

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\geq\max\left\{\binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}+1,\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-s}{k}-\binom{n-s-d}{k-1}+\binom{n-s-d}{k-d}\right\},
$$

**Sharp stability conjecture.** There exists $B\in[n]^{(s)}$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{F}\setminus\operatorname{OR}_B|\leq\binom{n-s-d}{k-d}.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the paper's stability theorem for the Erdős matching problem. The surrounding text identifies resolving the Erdős matching conjecture itself as the main open question and presents this as a further sharp stability problem.
object.source_name: David Ellis, Nathan Keller and Noam Lifshitz, “Stability versions of Erdős-Ko-Rado type theorems, via isoperimetry”, arXiv:1604.02160 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.02160

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2016).

object.title: Singleton-hypergraph extremal conjecture for the isolation lemma
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a hypergraph on vertex set $[n]$, let $M$ be a positive integer, and let $f$ be an objective function used to assign each edge its weight. Write $Z(H,M,f)$ for the set of isolating weights, and let $Y(M,n)$ denote the universal lower bound on $|Z(H,M,f)|$. The singleton hypergraph $S_n$ has vertex set $[n]$ and edges $\\{1\\},\dots,\\{n\\}$.

**Singleton-hypergraph extremal conjecture.**

$$
Y(M,n) = n\sum_{i=0}^{M-1} i^{n-1}
$$

The conjecture asserts that the singleton hypergraph, and equivalently its complementary hypergraph in the stated extremal count, gives the tight universal bound for the number of isolating weight functions.
object.source_name: Vance Faber and David G. Harris, “Tight bounds and conjectures for the isolation lemma”, arXiv:1604.07035 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07035

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2016).

object.title: Deep-hole classification conjecture for projective Reed–Solomon codes
object.statement:
Let $q$ be odd and $2\le k\le q-2$. Represent a word of $\mathbb{F}_q^{q+1}$ as $(u_f,v)$, where $u_f=(f(\alpha_1),\ldots,f(\alpha_q))$ is defined by a polynomial $f$ of degree at most $q-1$ and $v\in\mathbb{F}_q$.

**Projective deep-hole conjecture.** The set

$$
\{(u_f,v)\mid \deg(f)=k,\ v\in\mathbb{F}_q\}
$$

is precisely the set of all deep holes of $PRS(q+1,k)$.

The conjecture is stronger than the covering-radius conjecture and aims to classify every deep hole of these projective Reed–Solomon codes. The paper proves the assertion under additional hypotheses and gives partial exclusion results for words with $\deg(f)\ge k+1$.
object.source_name: Jun Zhang and Daqing Wan, “On Deep Holes of Projective Reed-Solomon Codes”, arXiv:1605.02423 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02423

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2016). “This conjecture remains open, but has been proved in if either $k+1\le p$ or $3\le q-p+1\le k+1\le q-2$.”

object.title: General covering-radius conjecture for longest MDS codes
object.statement:
Let $q$ be odd, and let $C$ be a linear MDS code with parameters $[q+1,k]$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Its covering radius is denoted by $\rho(C)$.

**General covering-radius conjecture.** For $2\le k\le q-2$,

$$
\rho(C)=q-k.
$$

This extends the covering-radius conjecture from projective Reed–Solomon codes to every MDS code of the longest conjecturally possible length $q+1$. It is known in several parameter ranges; the source notes that non-PRS MDS codes exist, so the claim does not follow formally from the projective Reed–Solomon case.
object.source_name: Jun Zhang and Daqing Wan, “On Deep Holes of Projective Reed-Solomon Codes”, arXiv:1605.02423 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02423

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2016). “This conjecture remains open, but has been proved in if either $k+1\le p$ or $3\le q-p+1\le k+1\le q-2$.”

object.title: Rectangularity conjecture for unitary factors of orbit q-Eulerian polynomials
object.statement:
Let $bbda=(bbda_1,dots,bbda_m)$ be a partition, and let $C_{bbda}(x,q)$ be its orbit $q$-Eulerian polynomial. A factor is **unitary** when it is a factor of the form $1+xq^j$. **Rectangularity conjecture.** The polynomial $C_{bbda}(x,q)$ has a unitary factor if and only if $bbda=(r^m)$ is a rectangle with $r$ odd and $m$ even. In that case,

$$
C_{r,m}(x,q)=(1+xq^{\frac{rm}{2}})C'_{r,m}(x,q),
$$

where $C'_{r,m}(x,q)$ has no unitary factor. This generalizes the established one-column factorization and the cited equal-part odd case, but the full assertion remains open.
object.source_name: Angela Carnevale and Christopher Voll, “Orbit Dirichlet series and multiset permutations”, arXiv:1607.01292 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.01292

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

object.title: Kotzig's cyclic tree decomposition conjecture
object.statement: Let $T$ be a tree with $n+1$ vertices, and identify the vertices of $K_{2n+1}$ with the integers modulo $2n+1$. A cyclic decomposition into copies of $T$ consists of the cyclic shifts of one copy of $T$ forming an edge decomposition. **Ringel--Kotzig conjecture.** For any $(n+1)$-vertex tree $T$, the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ can be cyclically decomposed into copies of $T$. This strengthens Ringel's conjecture by requiring the decomposition to arise from cyclic shifts, and remains open in the source's discussion.
object.source_name: Anna Adamaszek, Peter Allen, Codrut Grosu and Jan Hladky, “Almost all trees are almost graceful”, arXiv:1608.01577 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.01577

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2016).

object.title: Pivotto's finite excluded-minor conjecture for graphic or bicircular lift matroids
object.statement: Let $BL$ be the class of bicircular lift matroids, and let $\overline{BL}$ be the union of $BL$ with the class of graphic matroids. The class $\overline{BL}$ is minor-closed. **Pivotto's conjecture.** The class $\overline{BL}$ has a finite list of excluded minors. This conjecture concerns the structural characterization of matroids that are graphic or bicircular lift through excluded minors. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
object.source_name: Rong Chen, “The excluded minors for the class of matroids that are graphic or bicircular lift”, arXiv:1609.03049 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03049

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

object.title: The LS+-perfect graph conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write ${\rm STAB}(G)$ for its stable set polytope and ${\rm ASTAB}^*(G)$ for the polyhedral relaxation associated with joined a-perfect graphs. A graph is **${\rm LS}_+$-perfect** when ${\rm LS}_+(G)={\rm STAB}(G)$, where ${\rm LS}_+(G)$ is the Lovász–Schrijver positive semidefinite relaxation applied to ${\rm ESTAB}(G)$.

**${\rm LS}_+$-perfect graph conjecture.** A graph $G$ is ${\rm LS}_+$-perfect if and only if

$$
{\rm STAB}(G)={\rm ASTAB}^*(G).
$$

Equivalently, the conjecture asserts that ${\rm LS}_+$-perfect graphs coincide with joined a-perfect graphs, with ${\rm ASTAB}^*(G)$ serving as the corresponding polyhedral relaxation of ${\rm STAB}(G)$.
object.source_name: Silvia Bianchi, Mariana Escalante, Graciela Nasini and Annegret Wagler, “Lovász-Schrijver PSD-operator on Claw-Free Graphs”, arXiv:1612.02670 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.02670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

object.title: Topological Tree Alternative Conjecture for locally finite trees
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a locally finite tree, and write $S\equiv^{\sharp}T$ when $S$ and $T$ are mutually topological minors, meaning $S\leq^{\sharp}T$ and $T\leq^{\sharp}S$. Count the isomorphism classes of such trees $S$.

**Topological Tree Alternative Conjecture.** For a given locally finite tree $T$, the number of isomorphism classes of trees that are mutually topological minors with $T$ is either $1$ or $\mathfrak c$.

This is the topological-minor analogue of the Tree Alternative Conjecture. It gives a sharp alternative for the size of each mutual-topological-minor equivalence class, and the supplied text does not state that it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Jorge Bruno and Paul J. Szeptycki, “Locally finite trees and the topological minor relation”, arXiv:1705.04937 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04937

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

object.title: Cluster-critical class characterization of clustered chromatic number
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a minor-closed class of graphs, and let $k\geqslant 0$ be an integer. A graph class is **$k$-cluster critical** if it is obtained as a wedge-product of $v$ copies of $\mathcal{I}$ and $p$ copies of $\mathcal{P}$, in some order, with $v+2p=k+1$. **Cluster-critical conjecture.** 
$$
\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{M})\geqslant k+1
$$
 if and only if $\mathcal{G}\not\subseteq\mathcal{M}$ for some $k$-cluster critical class $\mathcal{G}$. This reformulates the preceding obstruction conjecture in terms of wedge-products and cluster-critical classes. The source presents it as a conjectural characterization; no general proof or refutation is given.
object.source_name: Sergey Norin, Alex Scott, Paul Seymour and David R. Wood, “Clustered Colouring in Minor-Closed Classes”, arXiv:1708.02370 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02370

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2017). “This conjecture is easy for $t\leq 4$, is equivalent to the 4-colour theorem for $t=5$, is true for $t=6$ , and is open for $t\geq 7$.”

object.title: Conjecture that every gaussoid is compatible with all quadrics in J_n
object.statement:
Let $J_n$ be the ideal whose quadrics include the trinomials defining compatibility of gaussoids, and let a **gaussoid** be a collection of almost-principal minors satisfying the gaussoid axioms. A gaussoid is **compatible** with a polynomial when the corresponding vanishing and nonvanishing pattern satisfies that polynomial.

**All-quadrics compatibility conjecture.** Every gaussoid is compatible with all quadrics in $J_n$, not just trinomials.

This conjecture proposes that compatibility with the quadratic relations of $J_n$ is already determined by the trinomial relations. The paper presents it as a direction for developing gaussoid theory in parallel with matroid theory; its resolution is not given here.
object.source_name: Tobias Boege, Alessio D'Alì, Thomas Kahle and Bernd Sturmfels, “The Geometry of Gaussoids”, arXiv:1710.07175 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07175

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2017). “This conjecture is false.”

object.title: Gallai-Ramsey formula for disjoint unions of paths on three vertices
object.statement:
Let $P_3$ denote the path on three vertices, and let $gr_k(K_3:n_1P_3, ldots,n_kP_3)$ be the corresponding multicolor Gallai-Ramsey number. For positive integers $k,n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_k$ with $n_1=\max\{n_i\}$, **the $P_3$ Gallai-Ramsey conjecture.**

$$
gr_k(K_3:n_1P_3,n_2P_3,\ldots,n_kP_3)=2n_1+1+\sum_{i=1}^k(n_i-1).
$$

This extends the known two-color Ramsey formula for copies of $P_3$ to general Gallai colorings, but the source does not report a resolution.
object.source_name: Haibo Wu, Colton Magnant, Pouria Salehi Nowbandegani and Suman Xia, “All partitions have small parts - Gallai-Ramsey numbers of bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1710.10455 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10455

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

object.title: A Wagner conjecture for transitive directed acyclic graphs
object.statement:
Let a **TDAG** be a transitive directed acyclic graph, let d-minor operations be the directed-minor operations for TDAGs, and let a class be **d-minor-closed** when it is closed under those operations. For a class $\mathcal{G}$ of TDAGs, let $G_1,\ldots,G_r$ be TDAGs.

**A Wagner conjecture for TDAGs.** Every d-minor-closed class $\mathcal{G}$ of TDAGs has a finite set of excluded TDAGs $R=\{G_1,\ldots,G_r\}$ such that

$$
G\in\mathcal{G}\quad\text{if and only if}\quad\text{no }G_i\in R\text{ is a d-minor of }G.
$$

This is the directed analogue of Wagner's conjecture for undirected graph minors. The supplied text presents it as a major question and gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
object.source_name: Argyrios Deligkas and Reshef Meir, “Directed Graph Minors and Serial-Parallel Width”, arXiv:1711.01806 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.01806

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

object.title: Reed's domination conjecture for connected cubic graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected cubic graph, and let $V(G)$ denote its vertex set. A **dominating set** is a subset of vertices such that every vertex outside the subset has a neighbor in it. **Reed's conjecture.** Every connected cubic graph $G$ contains a dominating set of at most

$$
\left\lceil \frac{|V(G)|}{3} \right\rceil
$$

vertices. This conjecture gives a universal upper bound on the domination number of connected cubic graphs; the source presents it as a statement that has been suggested and widely discussed, without supplying evidence of a resolution.
object.source_name: Misa Nakanishi, “Sufficient condition for Reed's conjecture”, arXiv:1809.08987 (2019).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1711.07587](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.07587).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08987

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

object.title: Lovász–Woodall conjecture on cycles through prescribed independent edges
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph, and let $S$ be a set of $k$ independent edges of $G$. Here, independent edges have no common endpoint.

**Lovász–Woodall conjecture.** If $k$ is even or $G-S$ is connected, then $G$ contains a cycle containing every edge in $S$.

This conjecture is part of the classical problem of finding cycles through prescribed edges. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Paul Knappe and Max Pitz, “Circuits through prescribed edges”, arXiv:1810.09323 (2018).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1707.07291](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.07291).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.09323

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

object.title: The Graham–Häggkvist tree decomposition conjecture
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ edges, and let $K_{n,n}$ be the balanced complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part.

**Graham–Häggkvist conjecture.** The edge set of $K_{n,n}$ can be decomposed into copies of every $n$-edge tree $T$.

This is the bipartite analogue of the tree-decomposition conjecture associated with Ringel. The source states that it remains open, although the paper discusses rainbow embedding approaches.
object.source_name: Alp Müyesser and Alexey Pokrovskiy, “On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture”, arXiv:2509.05280 (2025).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2008.00926](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00926), [arXiv:1607.01456](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.01456).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

object.title: Goddard–Henning conjecture on independent domination in cubic graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected cubic graph of order $n$, and let $i(G)$ denote its independent domination number. Reed's bound concerns domination in cubic graphs, and the exceptional graphs here are $K_{3,3}$ and the $5$-prism $C_5 \mathbin{\Box} K_2$.

**Goddard–Henning conjecture.** If

$$
G \notin \{K_{3,3}, C_5 \mathbin{\Box} K_2\},
$$

then

$$
i(G) \leq \frac{3}{8}n.
$$

The conjecture asks whether Reed's $\frac{3}{8}$ upper bound for the domination number extends to independent domination, apart from the two stated exceptions. The supplied source presents it as a conjecture; its resolution is not specified here.
object.source_name: Boštjan Brešar, Tanja Dravec and Michael A. Henning, “A proof of the 38-conjecture for independent domination in cubic graphs”, arXiv:2510.14762 (2025).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2303.09993](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09993), [arXiv:2001.02946](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02946), [arXiv:1708.01725](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01725).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14762

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025). “However despite the pleasing result given in Theorem , prior to this paper it remained an open problem to characterize the graphs achieving equality in Theorem .”
